signature: MACHT MICHAEL [master's mark: “M.N.” over bird; on bell, later stamp: BOHLAND & FUCHS / GRASLITZ / 8] NAGEL 1656
pitch: B-flat + 40 cents @ a = 440, B-flat + 5 cents (±A at Chorton) with slide extended approx. 44mm.
mouthpiece: Modern manufacture by Ursula Munzel in early style.
dimensions: bo 9.8 / 9.5, be 109, le 2659.5, diam. of mouthpipe 11.3, diam. of slide sec. exit 10, diam. of bell sec. entry12.2, diam. of neckpipe above first ferrule 11.9, diam. of neckpipe prior to bow 12.3, diam. of bellpipe after bow 11.9, total length of slide sec. 1659.5, total length of bell sec. 1046.5, overlap 28.5; mean bell thickness: immediately adjacent to garland 0.19; 100mm from rim 0.27.
provenance: Bohland & Fuchs, instrument makers, Graslitz (now Kraslice, Czech Republic)
remarks: Restored by Ursula Munzel, Munich. Flat bell stay with eyelet near bell-pipe side, decorated with young woman picking a flower. Tubular slide-stays, lower one telescopic. Ring in slide-bow. Slide sec. later, probably from early 18c. Bell at 4th pos. Muffled sound, apparently the result of an air leak; harmonics are out of tune in first pos. Examined by Carter, April 1997.
